T4.4.message: trimūrtim is marked as an epithet. The compound split and the gloss 'having three forms' are given in compounds.c1, and the note explains the wordplay (mūrti, 'form', is denied and then counted three times). Nothing in the data says what the three forms are. mw-trimurti.md gives 'having 3 forms or shapes (as Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva)'. shlokam-vedasara-shiva-stava.md glosses trimurti as 'the cosmic presence behind creation, sustenance and dissolution'. gitapress-stotraratnavali.md reads the line as the paradox 'मूर्तिहीन त्रिमूर्ति' (the formless One with three forms). The verse is playing on this word, so the reader may need to know which three forms are meant. A human should decide whether this gap is enough to fail.
T4.4.suggested_fix: Add one clause to words.w23.notes (en/hi), or to compounds.c1.note: the three forms are Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva, the One who creates, keeps and dissolves the world. So the One with no form of His own is praised as the One who takes all three.
